A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the L. acidophilis system at pH 5-5.5 is a puromycin-insensitive system.
L. acidophilis is a useful system for studies on the mechanism of cell-free protein biosynthesis and that it is particularly suitable for studies at acid pH.
the poly(U)-directed phenylalanineincorporation system of L. lactobacilli is not inhibited by puromycin at pH 5, and that the inhibition of the E. coli system is due to the effect of puromycylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
puromycin is not a general inhibitor of cell-free protein synthesizing systems.
L. acidophilis is a good model organism to study the effects of pH on protein synthesis and the effects of pH and puromycin on protein synthesis.
puromycin is not an effective inhibitor of polyuridylic-acid directed phenylalanine incorpora-tion by L. acidophillus at acid pH.
